title: Polynomial presentation of an arbitrary principal localization
statement:
theorem exists_localization_presentation
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
    (h : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) :
      let S := MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)
      let g : S := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ h
      let relations : Option (Fin c) → MvPolynomial (Option (Fin n)) R :=
        Option.elim' (MvPolynomial.rename some h * MvPolynomial.X none - 1)
          (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.rename some (f i))
      let T := MvPolynomial (Option (Fin n)) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range relations)
      ∃ e : T ≃ₐ[R] Localization.Away g,
        (∀ i : Fin n,
          e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X (some i))) =
            algebraMap S (Localization.Away g) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X i))) ∧
        e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X none)) = IsLocalization.Away.invSelf g

proof.text: Evaluate the old variables in S_g and the new variable at invSelf g. The renamed equations vanish by quotient membership, and h*X_none-1 vanishes by mul_invSelf. Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ gives forward : T →ₐ[R] S_g.

Rename the old variables into T. The old equations lie in the defining ideal, so Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ descends this map to base : S →ₐ[R] T. The added equation gives base(g)*[X_none]=1; thus base(g) is a unit. IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom extends base to backward : S_g →ₐ[R] T.

The extended map sends invSelf(g) to [X_none], by unit cancellation applied to the two inverse identities. The composite backward ∘ forward fixes each polynomial generator, hence is the identity by polynomial extensionality and quotient surjectivity. The composite forward ∘ backward fixes S, hence is the identity by localization extensionality. AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom combines the maps; evaluation of X_some and X_none gives the required formulas. No nontriviality or nonvanishing assumption is used.
